prediction: Chess champion: resolve the original deadline

prediction: Lighter and thinner portable computers
success_criteria: Material reduction in both weight and thickness versus turn-of-century notebooks; not a claim about every model.
assessment_explanation: Apple’s 2000 PowerBook weighed 5.7–6.1 lb, and its 2001 model was one inch thick. The 2008 MacBook Air weighed 3 lb and was at most 0.76 inch thick. These are contemporaneous manufacturer specifications supporting the qualitative trend before 2009.
limitations: The comparison is approximately the preceding decade, not a market-weighted 1999-versus-2009 average. “By 2008” is an evidence bound, not the first invention year.

prediction: Computers embedded in clothing and jewelry
success_criteria: Common adoption of computing embedded in the specified objects; a phone carried in a pocket is not automatically clothing integration.
assessment_explanation: The original scope is stronger than “smartphones exist.” The retrospective relies partly on counting carried devices. Independent adoption evidence for literal clothing/jewelry integration has not been established here.
limitations: Keep source-confirmed but unscored; do not import the earlier “achieved” rating.

prediction: At least a dozen body-networked computers
success_criteria: Define a separately countable computer and body network before testing population prevalence.
assessment_explanation: Counting chips inside a phone is not the same as counting independently networked worn devices. The legacy paraphrase removed both the numerical threshold and body-LAN condition. No stable counting convention is specified.
limitations: This is an intrinsic unit/scope ambiguity, not a claim that hardware progress stopped. A published counting convention could make it scorable later.

prediction: Personal devices largely without moving parts
success_criteria: Define the population of personal computers, then measure the proportion with no moving parts.
assessment_explanation: Phones and notebooks cannot be silently combined or separated to obtain a favorable majority. Apple’s 2008 Air still offered a hard disk as well as an SSD option. A sales/installed-base denominator is needed.

prediction: Most portable computers lack keyboards
success_criteria: Fix whether phones count as portable computers and whether virtual keyboards count, then measure majority adoption.
assessment_explanation: The input changed keyboard absence into touch/voice use. Those are not equivalent. The required 2009 device-population comparison is still missing.

prediction: Home and office servers for most users
success_criteria: Most users have the specified local storage servers; access to someone else’s cloud service is not a substitute.
assessment_explanation: The server/cloud distinction was blurred in the intake. The source is located, but no appropriate adoption denominator has been established. Missing evidence is not a WRONG verdict.

prediction: Wireless delivery of digital media and software
success_criteria: Real, deployed wireless file delivery for digital books, music, films and software without separately distributing physical objects.
assessment_explanation: Kindle offered wireless books and periodicals in 2007. Apple documented large-scale music and film downloads in 2008 and wireless application delivery over cellular/Wi-Fi that July. This verifies a digital-distribution capability, not a majority share of all books or media.
limitations: Remove the intake’s unsupported “mostly all media” strengthening. The corrected claim is narrower and has contemporary outcome support.

prediction: Wireless links replace some peripheral cables
success_criteria: Substantial replacement across the listed component types, not the disappearance of every cable.
assessment_explanation: Bluetooth keyboards and mice were shipping years before 2009. This supports meaningful substitution, but does not establish the whole range of links, including displays. The intake’s “cables will vanish” wording was too absolute.
limitations: The partial assessment is conservative. Broader peripheral adoption evidence could justify regrading the original trend claim.

prediction: Routine, reliable, high-bandwidth wireless access
success_criteria: Routine built-in wireless connectivity plus the reliability/availability promised; do not equate ever-use with dominance.
assessment_explanation: Built-in Wi-Fi was real, and Pew found 56% of US adults had ever used wireless Internet in 2009. Only 19% had used handheld Internet the previous day. This supports substantial use, not universal reliable high-bandwidth access.
limitations: US survey only. “The Web mainly wirelessly” is not the original claim and is not demonstrated by these figures.

prediction: Dictation creates the majority of text
success_criteria: More than half of text production uses dictation by the deadline; software availability alone does not qualify. The associated transcription-accuracy claim is retained as an unmeasured qualifier; failing the majority threshold is sufficient for the full conjunction to miss.
assessment_explanation: Kurzweil’s own retrospective expressly concedes the majority threshold was not reached. That is direct evidence of the historical deadline miss, though not an independent global usage survey. Subsequent speech-recognition progress cannot retroactively make 2009 an on-time hit.
limitations: Do not publish a numerical 2026 dictation share. This package confirms the deadline miss, not universal present-day nonfulfillment.

prediction: Ubiquitous language interfaces and animated assistants

assessment_explanation: The author’s retrospective acknowledges non-ubiquity while describing narrower implementations. Apple’s 2011 Siri launch is later evidence of a capable assistant, not proof that the full 2009 adoption claim was met.
limitations: The standalone Siri app preceded iPhone 4S. Do not use 2011 as the first-ever assistant date or automatically mark the whole forecast LATE.

prediction: Paper-like displays and routine electronic reading

assessment_explanation: The 2007 Kindle provided a paper-like electronic display and wireless books, newspapers and magazines. That establishes a substantial realization, but this review does not equate its 167-ppi display with every quality of paper or establish the full adoption scope.
limitations: No claim about a majority of book reading is established by this row.
